deviations.text: 6.1 debug: the vendored exp41 src/k3circuit.py and src/k3engine.py were last modified at 03:42:39Z, after data/validation_rows_C1forced.jsonl was written (02:38:29Z), so the 'unchanged vendored path' is not the code that produced the target 8.29053352355957. The ids and position classes are verified independently: the exp41 clean margins reproduce with 0.0 difference (S1, B3 and T10). Reproduced d = 8.3867 (|diff| 0.096 > 0.05); the held-out rerun proceeds with the final vendored code and the value is reported with this offset.

G1 engine check vs iteration-8 base_subarm margins misses 0.05 on some templates (instruct: exact 0.25/0.5-nat bf16 logit steps on 2-4 of 5 templates; base: up to 0.17 nats). base_subarm was computed by engine8 on a different card (its loader notes a 20 GB GPU and a CPU embedding table), while exp41 (L4, same as here) reproduces exactly (max |diff| 0.0 on all 40 B2 prompts). Reproduction offsets are recorded per template in results/capture_*.json; no engine is mixed.

Confirmation signal 'RS-fork(36) closes about 1.0 of the gap' failed on the first prompts (B3 0.44-0.58, T10 -0.42 to 0.50). The identity check passes (all components patched = RS-fork(36) within 0.06), so the patch is not broken: RS-fork(36) swaps the residual but keeps the INSTRUCT final norm and unembedding, which themselves carry a large part of the gap (readout change). Debugged rather than stopped: a CPU readout decomposition (analysis9.readout_decomposition) is added and every share is also reported relative to RS-fork(36) (labelled supplementary).

First B2 pass (v1, archived in results/v1_variable_batch/) used variable last-chunk batch shapes and full-forward caches: self-patch |dm| up to 0.22 and batched-vs-single dm differences up to 0.21 nats (G2/G4 failed). Per the fallback, the primary rerun (v2) uses a fixed batch shape (40 one-token rows, 8 full-forward rows, padded) and fork values captured on the same one-token path (onetok_capture) for both models; anchors m_I and m_B are the one-token-path margins.
S6 (B3) runs in its own instruct load (b3_9.py gpu) rather than inside S3's load.
analysis9.py was written after COMMIT #0; its sha256 is committed in commit0b before any verdict is computed. Verdict rules and thresholds are in COMMIT #0.
FPD is applied at the counterfactual fork token only (base logits at that one position), not at every entropy-gated position as in Cantarero et al. (plan departure f).

In generation, FSTACK / RAND patches act on the fork position's forward pass, so the K/V cached at that position carry the patch; every later position is computed by the unpatched instruct model. FPD rows keep the instruct K/V at the fork and only replace its sampling distribution.
Generation uses, per template, the first B2 prompt of that template (cached base values exist only for the B2 prompts) x 6 CRN slots (seeds 9101-9130), 30 programs per arm and unit.

When a type's candidate pool is exhausted (MLP pools hold 3-5 components), the no-repeat rule falls back to the full pool, so a few random sets contain a repeated MLP (e.g. T10 set 13 has MLP L31 twice) and patch 9 distinct components; distinct-draw counts are in random_sets.json.

G2 (self-patch |dm| <= 0.02) still fails in v2 (max 0.11 MST, 0.15 CC; mean share 0.003 / 0.001): head writes are cached in bf16, so setting a head's write to its own cached value re-rounds it; MLP and attention-output patches are exact (identity ALL_attn - RS36 = 0.0). G4 (batched vs single) passes exactly (0.0).
G-T04 and G-R6 have 5 prompts each (prompts8 holds only the W1-W5 twins, no noun variants), so their CIs are crude (plan departure b).

L-GRID: every prompt fails the committed on-policy rule (instruct log P(opening) about -13.6 < -5 over the 52-token opening), so Llama is reported descriptively and excluded from the B1 verdict; L-SP (shortest path) was not run (second in the drop order).
Token maps for unmapped base fork tokens (forced instruct continuations) were not built; the unmapped base mass is reported (G-GRID 0.66, G-T04 0.16, G-R6 0.31/0.34).
